source_snapshot.procedure: In BMC WebUI Hardware status > Inventory and LEDs, check Chassis information and detail information.
source_snapshot.criteria: Data should be readable and correct.
source_snapshot.deepseek: YES assumes FirmwareInventory is an inline array, OR-matches any Name containing SMC or FPGA, disables TLS verification and omits collection member traversal, topology, lifecycle and actual WebUI evidence.
source_snapshot.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION correctly requires exact SMC_FPGA component mapping, complete active/staged lifecycle evidence and no-update controls, but treats finite topology/version inputs as a continuing decision.

old_problem: FirmwareInventory can contain multiple controllers and programmable devices with overlapping SMC/FPGA names. An OR-substring result can select several wrong targets, and a collection normally requires Members link traversal rather than an assumed inline array. The old review fixed the evidence model but retained Pending for Project mapping/lifecycle/version inputs in an inventory-only case.
disposition_reason: Enumerate the complete advertised firmware/software inventory, bind exactly one Project SMC FPGA through durable component/topology relationships rather than name matching, separate active/running, backup and staged images under approved vendor lifecycle semantics, and reconcile complete inventory with the actual WebUI and Project firmware matrix. No update, activation, rollback or reset is authorized.
decision_basis: XLSX row 966, same-row DeepSeek, exact GPT V2, tests JSON, selection manifest, historical V3.1 record and adjacent row 967 were directly reviewed; next pending was verified as Functionality row 967 / variant ae345a0212f14b9f.
A standard Redfish collection exposes member links and may paginate; `.FirmwareInventory[]` is not a portable collection shape. Each member must be retrieved and preserved before target selection.

SoftwareInventory provides component identity/version/status/updateability evidence, but SMC_FPGA physical ownership and active/backup/staged roles are vendor/Project semantics and cannot be inferred from a substring, first result or highest version.
The Master requires actual WebUI chassis/detail evidence. Firmware JSON is supporting evidence and cannot replace the rendered SMC_FPGA presentation.

ED-02, ED-03, ED-07, ED-08, ED-12, ED-17, ED-19, ED-21 and ED-30 preserve exact target/lifecycle/evidence boundaries; ED-33 through ED-38 and ED-44 permit read-only parameterization while separating inventory from update coverage.

test_case.test_name: Validate exact SMC FPGA firmware identity and active/staged lifecycle inventory
test_case.purpose: Verify the exact Project-defined SMC FPGA component is uniquely represented in complete BMC firmware inventory, its component identity, active/running and any backup/staged version, health/state and updateability metadata match the approved lifecycle matrix, and the actual WebUI shows consistent information without executing any firmware or management-plane change.
required_package: Immutable SUT/BMC/platform/firmware/WebUI identity and approved SMC FPGA physical/control-plane topology with durable component ID/association
Service-root-discovered UpdateService/FirmwareInventory or approved SoftwareInventory collection, supported schema versions, pagination and complete member access
Authoritative member-to-SMC-FPGA association using durable SoftwareId, related component/topology link or approved vendor identifier; Name substring is locator-only
Vendor lifecycle model defining active/running, backup, staged, pending activation, unsupported and stale records plus expected uniqueness
Approved firmware matrix with expected active and allowed backup/staged Version, VersionScheme, component identity, Status.State/Health and Updateable semantics
Actual WebUI Inventory and LEDs SMC_FPGA row/detail mapping, trusted TLS/protected credentials, evidence freshness/redaction and no-update audit controls
test_case.test_command: READ ONLY. Verify immutable target and discover UpdateService/FirmwareInventory or the approved SoftwareInventory link from the Redfish service. Traverse every collection page and every `Members[].@odata.id`, preserving complete redacted member records; do not expect an inline FirmwareInventory array. Locate candidates by name only if needed, then bind exactly one SMC FPGA through the approved durable SoftwareId/topology/component relationship and explicitly reject unrelated SMC or FPGA entries. Record Id/Name, SoftwareId, Version, VersionScheme, Status.State/Health, Updateable, ReleaseDate, LowestSupportedVersion and related/OEM lifecycle fields when supported. Interpret active/running, backup and staged/pending roles only through the approved vendor model and compare each role with its own Project expectation. Capture the actual rendered BMC WebUI Inventory and LEDs SMC_FPGA row/detail and reconcile component, version, lifecycle and health within freshness tolerance. Repeat read fingerprints only; never upload firmware, invoke SimpleUpdate/Multipart/HttpPushUri, activate, roll back, reset, reboot, power-cycle or clear logs.
test_case.expected_result: Complete inventory traversal yields exactly one approved SMC FPGA component relationship, with no ambiguous/duplicate or unrelated substring match. Its active/running version and state/health exactly match the Project baseline; any backup/staged/pending record is separately identified and matches its own allowed lifecycle/version rather than being credited as active. Supported metadata is schema-valid, actual WebUI evidence reconciles within freshness tolerance, no expected member is missing and no firmware/management/DUT state changes.
test_case.pass_fail_basis: PASS requires complete paginated member traversal, exact topology-backed target binding, explicit lifecycle roles, exact expected version/health/updateability comparison and actual rendered WebUI parity. An SMC-or-FPGA substring, first/highest version, collection HTTP success or version-only response cannot pass. Missing/duplicate/ambiguous component, staged version treated as active, unexplained null/unknown/unsupported state, WebUI/API mismatch or wrong expected version is FAIL. Missing component map/lifecycle/version matrix is NOT READY rather than Pending; no version threshold is invented.
safety_gate: Use only certificate-verified protected GET/read operations discovered from the service; do not expose credentials or follow any UpdateService action/write link.
Bind the exact SMC FPGA by approved durable component/topology identity; name substring is candidate discovery only and cannot establish target identity.
Keep active/running, backup, staged and pending-activation records distinct under documented target semantics; do not choose highest/first version heuristically.
Prohibit firmware upload, SimpleUpdate, MultipartHttpPushUri, HttpPushUri, activation, rollback, SCM/FPGA reset, BMC reset, reboot, power action and log clearing.
Retain complete raw collection/member artifacts and actual rendered WebUI evidence before normalization/redaction, including unsupported/null fields.
Stop on incomplete pagination, duplicate target, unknown lifecycle, credential exposure or API/UI disagreement and do not automatically retry with an update/reset.
expected_evidence: Immutable target and approved SMC FPGA topology/durable component map plus service/collection/schema identity
Complete paginated FirmwareInventory/SoftwareInventory member list and full protected raw record for every target-related member
Normalized SMC FPGA lifecycle matrix with durable identity, active/running, backup/staged, Version/VersionScheme, Status/Health, Updateable and exact Project comparison
Actual rendered WebUI Inventory and LEDs SMC_FPGA row/detail visual artifacts with component/version/lifecycle parity timestamps
Explicit rejection of unrelated SMC/FPGA substring candidates and accounting for null/unsupported/stale fields
Pre/post inventory fingerprints, preserved SEL/audit logs, no-update/no-activate/no-reset/no-power proof and engineer verdict
test_case.recovery: No mutation is intended. On incomplete collection, ambiguous component mapping, unknown lifecycle, version mismatch or API/UI disagreement, stop and preserve/redact evidence and obtain the authoritative topology/lifecycle matrix. Do not upload, activate, roll back, reset, reboot, power-cycle, clear logs or automatically retry.

source_conflict.reason: Master consistently requests readable/correct SMC_FPGA information in WebUI. The broad DeepSeek substring and assumed collection shape are incomplete implementation guidance, not a conflicting target.

blocked.reason: Exact-target read-only firmware inventory is technically defined. Component topology, lifecycle semantics and expected versions are bounded Project prerequisites.

pending.remaining_project_configuration: SMC FPGA durable component/topology map; actual inventory collection/schema; active/backup/staged lifecycle semantics; expected versions/health/updateability; WebUI mapping; trust, freshness and redaction.
pending.execution_status: NOT STARTED; READ-ONLY SMC_FPGA FIRMWARE INVENTORY ONLY; NO REDFISH, WEBUI, UPDATE, RESET, POWER OR DUT ACTION EXECUTED

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Resource and Schema Guide 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Defines UpdateService, SoftwareInventory/FirmwareInventory collection traversal and component Version, VersionScheme, Status and Updateable fields used for the read-only lifecycle matrix.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Data Model Specification 2025.3
external_authorities.application: Provides normative SoftwareInventory and collection data-model semantics; vendor mapping is still required to associate members with the physical SMC FPGA and lifecycle roles.

external_authorities.title: DMTF Redfish Schema Index
external_authorities.application: Provides the authoritative schema/version resources used to validate the target-advertised UpdateService and SoftwareInventory payloads.

project_authority: The Project/vendor package binds the exact SMC FPGA to durable inventory members, defines lifecycle roles and supplies expected active/backup/staged versions. Those finite inputs make inventory fully automatable but never authorize a firmware action.
